title: Green Mentorship Programme 2026: Launch Your Career in Sustainability and Climate Action in Cairo
summary: The Green Mentorship Programme is inviting senior university students and recent graduates to participate in an exciting career development session designed to help aspiring sustainability professionals begin their journey in one of the world s fastest-growing sectors. If you are passionate about sustainability, climate change, environmental protection, and sustainable development, this programme offers an excellent opportunity to gain valuable insights into career pathways while learning directly from professionals working in the field. As governments, businesses, and international organizations continue to prioritize environmental sustainability and climate resilience, the demand for professionals equipped with sustainability knowledge is increasing rapidly. The Green Mentorship Programme has been created to bridge the gap between academic learning and professional practice by introducing participants to the skills, knowledge, and opportunities needed to succeed in the sustainability sector. Whether your goal is to work with international organizations, environmental NGOs, private companies, research institutions, or public sector agencies, this mentorship session can help you better understand the industry and prepare for future career opportunities. About the Green Mentorship Programme The Green Mentorship Programme is a career-focused initiative designed to support students and recent graduates who want to build successful careers in sustainability and climate action. The programme provides participants with an opportunity to learn about emerging sustainability trends, explore career options, and gain practical advice on entering this competitive and impactful field. Rather than focusing only on theoretical knowledge, the programme emphasizes practical guidance that can help participants confidently navigate the transition from university to professional employment within the sustainability sector. Why Sustainability Careers Matter Sustainability has become one of the most important global priorities across industries. Organizations around the world are investing heavily in environmental protection, renewable energy, climate adaptation, sustainable development, and responsible business practices. As a result, professionals with sustainability knowledge are increasingly sought after in sectors such as: Environmental consulting Renewable energy Climate policy Corporate sustainability Sustainable finance International development Green technology Circular economy initiatives Environmental education Non-governmental organizations (NGOs) Government agencies Research institutions The Green Mentorship Programme aims to prepare young professionals to take advantage of these growing opportunities. What Participants Will Learn During the mentorship session, participants will gain valuable knowledge and practical insights into the sustainability industry. Key learning areas include: 1. Introduction to Sustainability Participants will explore important sustainability concepts and understand why environmental and social sustainability are becoming essential across industries. 2. Climate Change and Global Development The programme will examine how climate change is influencing economies, societies, businesses, and international development efforts. 3. Emerging Career Opportunities Attendees will discover various career pathways available in sustainability, including opportunities in the public sector, private companies, nonprofit organizations, and international institutions. 4. Practical Career Guidance Participants will receive useful advice on: Starting a sustainability career Building relevant skills Preparing for future opportunities Understanding employer expectations Identifying growth areas within the green economy Benefits of Attending Participants can expect several valuable benefits from joining the Green Mentorship Programme, including: Better understanding of sustainability careers. Exposure to emerging environmental and climate-related professions. Practical guidance for entering the sustainability sector. Increased awareness of global sustainability challenges. Opportunities to connect with individuals who share similar interests. Career development support for students and graduates. Enhanced knowledge of sustainability and climate action. Who Should Attend? The programme is specifically designed for: Senior university students. Recent graduates. Individuals interested in sustainability. Young people passionate about climate action. Aspiring professionals seeking careers in environmental and development sectors. Applicants from different academic backgrounds are encouraged to participate if they have an interest in sustainability. Session Details Participants should note the following event information: Location Founder s Space Cairo, Egypt Date 8 August 2026 Time 10:00 AM – 3:00 PM The session will be conducted in person, providing participants with opportunities to engage directly with mentors and fellow attendees. Why You Should Participate Attending the Green Mentorship Programme offers an excellent opportunity to gain early exposure to one of the world s most rapidly expanding career sectors. By participating, you will be able to: Explore sustainability career pathways. Learn directly from experienced professionals. Build knowledge relevant to future employment. Strengthen your understanding of climate action. Expand your professional network. Prepare for future career opportunities in the green economy. How to Apply Interested applicants should complete the official registration form by providing the required information, including: Full name Age Gender Email address Phone number Field of study or work Governorate A brief response explaining what they expect to learn from the session Applicants are encouraged to register early, as spaces for in-person events may be limited. Application Deadline No application deadline has been specified. Interested participants should register as soon as possible before the session date of 8 August 2026 to secure a place. APPLY HERE For more mentorship programs visit OFY Website HERE Conclusion The Green Mentorship Programme is an excellent opportunity for senior university students and recent graduates who aspire to build meaningful careers in sustainability and climate action. Through expert guidance, practical career advice, and exposure to emerging opportunities in the green economy, participants will gain valuable insights that can help shape their professional future. If you are passionate about creating positive environmental and social impact while pursuing a rewarding career, this programme offers an ideal starting point. Register early to ensure your participation in this valuable in-person learning experience in Cairo. title: Wissenschaftskolleg Early Career Fellowship 2027/2028 in Germany: Fully Funded Research Opportunity for Humanities and Social Sciences Scholars
summary: The Wissenschaftskolleg zu Berlin (Institute for Advanced Study) has officially opened applications for its prestigious Early Career Fellowship for the 2027/2028 academic year. This internationally recognized fellowship offers early-career researchers in the humanities and social sciences a unique opportunity to dedicate ten months exclusively to their own research in one of Europe s leading interdisciplinary academic environments. Designed to give scholars the freedom to think, write, collaborate, and develop groundbreaking ideas without the distractions of regular teaching or administrative responsibilities, the fellowship brings together researchers from different disciplines and countries to encourage intellectual exchange and innovation. If you are an emerging researcher seeking uninterrupted time to advance your academic work while engaging with an international community of distinguished scholars, this fellowship presents an exceptional opportunity. About the Wissenschaftskolleg Fellowship The Wissenschaftskolleg zu Berlin, also known as the Institute for Advanced Study, is one of the world s leading institutes dedicated to promoting advanced research across disciplines. Every year, it welcomes scholars from different parts of the world to pursue independent research while participating in an intellectually vibrant academic community. Unlike many traditional research programs, the Wissenschaftskolleg places great emphasis on academic freedom. Fellows are encouraged to pursue research topics of their own choosing rather than being assigned specific institutional projects. This approach allows researchers to explore innovative ideas, challenge existing perspectives, and produce impactful scholarship within a collaborative environment. Fellowship Duration Successful applicants will spend approximately 10 months at the Wissenschaftskolleg. The fellowship runs from: September 2027 Until the end of June 2028 Throughout this period, fellows will reside in Berlin and focus entirely on their independent research projects. What Makes This Fellowship Unique? One of the defining characteristics of the Wissenschaftskolleg Fellowship is its commitment to interdisciplinary collaboration. Rather than grouping researchers only by subject area, the institute intentionally brings together scholars from different academic disciplines. This diverse environment creates opportunities for: Cross-disciplinary collaboration Intellectual exchange New research perspectives Innovative thinking Academic networking International cooperation Long-term scholarly partnerships The institute believes that interactions between researchers from different fields often generate new questions, fresh approaches, and unexpected discoveries. Freedom to Pursue Independent Research At the heart of the fellowship is complete academic independence. Rather than prescribing research themes, the Wissenschaftskolleg encourages fellows to develop and pursue their own research questions. Participants can: Advance ongoing research Begin entirely new projects Write books or journal articles Complete major academic manuscripts Develop interdisciplinary collaborations Explore innovative methodologies This freedom allows scholars to make meaningful contributions to their fields while benefiting from an inspiring research environment. Fellowship Expectations Although fellows enjoy significant academic freedom, there are a few important responsibilities. Successful fellows are expected to: Reside at the Wissenschaftskolleg throughout the fellowship period. Participate in the institute s scholarly community. Join the daily communal meal, which serves as an important opportunity for informal academic discussions. Attend the weekly Tuesday Colloquium where fellows present ideas, discuss research, and engage in interdisciplinary conversations. These activities are central to the institute s collaborative philosophy and contribute to the vibrant intellectual atmosphere experienced by all fellows. Academic Environment The Wissenschaftskolleg is internationally recognized for fostering a stimulating research community where scholars can exchange ideas beyond the boundaries of their individual disciplines. Benefits of this environment include: Daily interaction with internationally renowned researchers Exposure to diverse academic perspectives Constructive feedback on research Opportunities for collaboration across disciplines A supportive and intellectually engaging community Time and space for uninterrupted research The institute believes that productive academic discussions often emerge from interactions between researchers with different expertise and viewpoints. Who Should Apply? The fellowship is specifically designed for researchers who are in the early stages of their academic careers and are working within the humanities or social sciences. Ideal applicants include scholars who: Have demonstrated strong academic potential. Are pursuing innovative research. Can contribute meaningfully to an interdisciplinary scholarly community. Wish to dedicate substantial time to independent research. Are interested in collaborating with researchers from around the world. Fields Covered The Early Career Call focuses on research within: Humanities Social Sciences Researchers from a broad range of disciplines within these fields are encouraged to submit applications. Application Process Interested candidates must submit their applications through the official online application portal provided by the Wissenschaftskolleg. Applicants should carefully review the eligibility requirements and application guidelines before submitting their materials. Application Steps Review the fellowship eligibility criteria. Prepare your research proposal. Gather all required application documents. Complete the online application form. Submit your application before the deadline. Application Deadline Deadline: 1 September 2026 Applicants are strongly encouraged to submit their applications well before the closing date to avoid any last-minute technical issues. APPLY HERE Important Information Applicants should note the following: The fellowship is intended for the 2027/2028 academic year. Fellows must reside at the Wissenschaftskolleg for approximately ten months. Daily communal meals and weekly Tuesday colloquia form part of the fellowship experience. Scholars have the freedom to pursue research projects of their own choice. The fellowship emphasizes interdisciplinary interaction among researchers. For more information visit the Wissenschaftskolleg website HERE For more fellowship programs visit OFY Website HERE Why You Should Consider Applying This fellowship offers far more than research funding or institutional affiliation. It provides an environment where scholars can: Focus entirely on research. Expand international academic networks. Collaborate with experts from diverse disciplines. Refine research ideas through intellectual exchange. Produce high-impact scholarly work. Gain recognition through association with one of the world s leading Institutes for Advanced Study. For ambitious early-career researchers seeking uninterrupted time to advance their scholarship, the Wissenschaftskolleg Fellowship represents a remarkable opportunity. How to Apply Applications must be submitted through the official Wissenschaftskolleg online application portal before the deadline. Prospective applicants interested in future fellowship cycles may also contact the institute via email to receive notifications about subsequent calls for applications. Conclusion The Wissenschaftskolleg Early Career Fellowship 2027/2028 offers an outstanding opportunity for emerging scholars in the humanities and social sciences to advance their research within a globally respected interdisciplinary environment. By providing ten months of dedicated research time, academic freedom, and meaningful engagement with an international community of scholars, the fellowship creates the ideal conditions for intellectual growth and scholarly excellence. Early-career researchers with ambitious research projects should take advantage of this prestigious opportunity and ensure their applications are submitted before 1 September 2026 . title: UNESCO and LG AI Research Launch Free Global Ethics of Artificial Intelligence Course on Coursera: Earn a Certificate While Learning
summary: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is transforming every sector of society—from healthcare and education to finance, governance, agriculture, manufacturing, and scientific research. As AI systems become increasingly integrated into everyday life, ensuring that they are developed and used responsibly has become one of the world s most pressing priorities. Recognizing this global need, UNESCO , in partnership with LG AI Research and Coursera , has officially launched the Global MOOC on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence , a free online course designed to help learners around the world understand and apply ethical principles throughout the AI lifecycle. Announced during the Ethics by Design: Industry and Innovation Conference held in Seoul, Republic of Korea, this globally accessible Massive Open Online Course (MOOC) represents an important milestone in transforming international AI ethics standards into practical knowledge that professionals, students, policymakers, researchers, and organizations can apply in real-world situations. Hosted on Coursera and available free of charge, the course equips learners with practical frameworks, case studies, and decision-making tools that support the responsible development, deployment, and governance of AI technologies. About the Global MOOC on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence The Global MOOC on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence has been created to translate the principles contained in UNESCO s Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence into practical learning experiences. Rather than simply explaining ethical concepts, the course demonstrates how these principles can be implemented throughout every stage of AI development—from system design and model training to deployment, governance, monitoring, and long-term societal impact. The course serves as a global public educational resource that allows learners everywhere to develop the practical skills needed to build trustworthy, transparent, fair, and human-centered AI systems. Official Launch of the Course The course was officially launched on 20 July 2026 during the Ethics by Design: Industry and Innovation Conference held at the Korean National Commission for UNESCO in Seoul. The launch ceremony brought together distinguished representatives from international organizations, governments, industry, academia, and AI research communities. Among those present were: Prof. Khaled El-Enany, Director-General of UNESCO Dr. Kyung Hoon Bae, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Science and ICT, Republic of Korea Dr. Woohyung Lim, Head of LG AI Research The event also welcomed: Government leaders Technology experts University researchers Industry professionals Members of the International Advisory Group Module leaders responsible for developing the course The gathering reflected the growing international collaboration required to ensure AI technologies remain ethical, inclusive, transparent, and beneficial to humanity. Built on UNESCO s Global AI Ethics Recommendation One of the defining strengths of this MOOC is that it is based directly on the UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence , adopted unanimously in 2021 by all 193 UNESCO Member States . This Recommendation became the world s first global normative framework dedicated specifically to AI ethics. Rather than functioning as a theoretical document, the Recommendation establishes internationally agreed principles covering: Human rights Human dignity Fairness Transparency Accountability Privacy Environmental sustainability Inclusiveness Safety Responsible governance The new course helps learners operationalize these principles in everyday professional practice. Why This Course Matters Artificial Intelligence is advancing rapidly across industries, creating both tremendous opportunities and significant ethical challenges. Organizations increasingly require professionals who understand not only how AI systems work but also how they should be designed and governed responsibly. According to UNESCO, ethical AI cannot be achieved through principles alone—it depends on people who possess the skills to apply those principles during every phase of AI development. This course bridges the gap between policy and practice by providing learners with practical tools to: Build trustworthy AI systems Identify ethical risks Balance innovation with responsibility Protect human rights Improve transparency Promote accountability Support inclusive AI development Make informed ethical decisions Who Should Take This Course? The MOOC has been designed for a broad global audience. It is suitable for: Artificial intelligence professionals Machine learning engineers Software developers AI researchers Data scientists University students Academic researchers Government policymakers Public administrators Technology executives Product managers Ethics specialists Innovation leaders Business professionals Anyone interested in understanding responsible AI No matter the learner s background, the course provides practical knowledge applicable across multiple industries. What You Will Learn Participants will gain practical understanding of responsible AI development through ten comprehensive learning modules. Learners will understand: Ethical AI principles Responsible AI design Human-centered AI development AI governance Privacy protection Transparency mechanisms Risk management Accountability frameworks Sustainable AI practices Fair AI decision-making The course emphasizes real-world implementation rather than theoretical discussion alone. Apply here Course Structure: Ten Comprehensive Modules The curriculum is organized into ten carefully designed modules covering the most important dimensions of AI ethics. Major topics include: 1. Fairness and Inclusion Learners explore methods for reducing bias in AI systems while promoting fairness and equitable outcomes. Topics include: Algorithmic bias Inclusive datasets Equal treatment Social equity 2. Privacy and Data Governance This module examines responsible data collection, management, protection, and governance. Topics include: Data privacy Consent Responsible data use Governance policies Data security 3. Transparency and Accountability Participants learn how organizations can make AI systems understandable and accountable. Key concepts include: Explainable AI Transparency reporting Accountability mechanisms Documentation Responsible oversight 4. Safety and Security The course explores methods for designing AI systems that remain safe, secure, and reliable. Topics include: Risk assessment AI safety Cybersecurity System reliability Responsible deployment 5. Environmental Sustainability Learners examine how AI development affects the environment and explore strategies to reduce environmental impacts. Topics include: Energy-efficient AI Sustainable computing Environmental responsibility Green AI practices 6. Global AI Governance Participants study international governance models and regulatory approaches shaping AI worldwide. Areas covered include: International cooperation AI regulation Global standards Public policy Governance frameworks 7–10. Practical Ethics Throughout the AI Lifecycle Across the remaining modules, learners engage with: Practical ethical decision-making Everyday AI development trade-offs Real-world case studies Reflection exercises Ethics-by-design methodologies Responsible innovation frameworks Practical Learning Experience Unlike many introductory AI ethics courses, this MOOC places strong emphasis on application. Learners will work with: Practical scenarios Interactive exercises Real-world examples Reflective learning activities Ethical decision-making frameworks Industry case studies The objective is to help participants confidently apply ethical principles in their own organizations and projects. Developed Through Global Collaboration The course represents a significant public-private partnership. It has been co-developed by: UNESCO LG AI Research Coursera Its curriculum has also been shaped by independent international AI experts representing leading academic and research institutions worldwide. This diverse collaboration ensures that the examples, perspectives, and case studies reflect different regional, cultural, and professional contexts. Visit here for more details on UNESCO and LG AI Research Launch Free Global Ethics of Artificial Intelligence Course on Coursera Expert Perspectives During the launch, UNESCO Director-General Prof. Khaled El-Enany emphasized that ethical AI depends on people who can translate shared principles into everyday practice. Dr. Kyung Hoon Bae highlighted the Republic of Korea s commitment to supporting human-centered AI development and digital inclusion through continued collaboration with UNESCO and the international community. Dr. Woohyung Lim of LG AI Research stressed that while international consensus on ethical AI already exists, the real challenge is embedding ethics throughout the entire AI lifecycle—from product development to operational deployment. Coursera Chief Content Officer Marni Baker Stein noted that the platform is proud to host the course, expanding access to high-quality education on responsible AI for learners worldwide. Industry Dialogue on Ethical AI The launch event also featured expert panel discussions involving representatives from: LG AI Research United Nations University Institute in Macau University of Toronto Korea AI Safety Institute Gwangju Institute of Science and Technology Kakao Naver Agence Francophone et Africaine de l Intelligence Artificielle (AFRIA) The discussions emphasized several key priorities: Building trustworthy AI Strengthening AI safety Improving fairness and accountability Embedding ethics into everyday product development Establishing strong governance structures Protecting human rights Communicating transparently with the public Certification Learners who successfully complete the course are eligible to receive a Coursera certificate , demonstrating their understanding of responsible AI and ethical AI principles. This certificate can strengthen professional profiles for individuals working in technology, public policy, research, education, business, and digital transformation. Language Availability The course is delivered primarily in English . To promote inclusive global participation, translation options are available in 11 languages , enabling learners from diverse linguistic backgrounds to benefit from the program. Cost The Global MOOC on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence is completely free to access through Coursera. This makes high-quality education on AI ethics accessible to learners regardless of geographic location or financial circumstances. Application Deadline There is no application deadline mentioned. The course is freely available on Coursera for learners worldwide. Why You Should Enroll This course offers an outstanding opportunity to understand one of the most important dimensions of artificial intelligence in today s digital world. Whether you are building AI systems, regulating them, researching new technologies, managing AI projects, or simply seeking to understand responsible innovation, the course provides practical tools grounded in internationally recognized ethical standards. With AI rapidly transforming industries worldwide, professionals who understand ethical AI principles will be increasingly valuable across both public and private sectors. Conclusion The UNESCO and LG AI Research Global MOOC on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence is more than just an online course—it is a global educational initiative aimed at ensuring AI serves humanity responsibly, fairly, and sustainably. Built upon UNESCO s internationally recognized Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence, the course transforms global ethical principles into practical skills that learners can immediately apply throughout the AI lifecycle. Freely available through Coursera and accessible worldwide, the program offers a unique opportunity for students, professionals, policymakers, researchers, developers, and organizations to deepen their understanding of responsible AI while earning a certificate from one of the world s leading online learning platforms. As artificial intelligence continues to reshape society, this course equips learners with the knowledge and practical frameworks needed to build trustworthy, transparent, human-centered AI systems that align innovation with ethical responsibility. title: Doctoral Researcher in the Social Sciences at the University of Helsinki 2026: Fully Funded PhD Opportunity on Migration, Platform Work and Digital Labor in Finland
summary: Are you passionate about migration studies, sociology, digital platforms, labor research, or social sciences? The University of Helsinki is inviting applications for a Doctoral Researcher in the Social Sciences position under the prestigious MAPS (Mapping Fragmented Labor in the Platformised Service Sector through Migrant Epistemologies) research project. This is an excellent opportunity for aspiring researchers to pursue a fully funded doctoral project while contributing to cutting-edge research on platform work, migration, and the transformation of labor in Finland. The position is hosted by the Swedish School of Social Sciences at the University of Helsinki and is funded by the Research Council of Finland . Successful applicants will receive funding for 3.5 years , beginning 1 October 2026 , while working alongside leading researchers and completing an article-based PhD. About the University of Helsinki Doctoral Research Position The University of Helsinki is one of Europe s leading research universities, known for excellence in teaching, innovation, and interdisciplinary research. This doctoral position forms part of the MAPS research project , led by Dr. Olivia Maury , which investigates how digital platforms are transforming service-sector labor through the experiences of migrant workers. The project seeks to understand the growing influence of platform technologies on work, employment, and migration while producing new knowledge that informs policy, academia, and society. The doctoral researcher will become part of a collaborative research environment while conducting independent doctoral research aligned with the project s objectives. About the MAPS Research Project Understanding Platformized Labor Through Migration Digital platforms have fundamentally transformed labor markets around the world. Increasingly, employment is characterized by: Temporary work Gig-based employment Multiple job holding Short-term task-based work Platform-mediated employment Blurred boundaries between paid and unpaid labor The MAPS project investigates these changes by focusing specifically on migrant workers operating within Finland s platform economy. Rather than studying labor solely from traditional employment perspectives, the project explores how migration, digitalization, and platform technologies interact to reshape working life. Research Focus The project aims to understand: How digital platforms reshape everyday working life. How migrants experience platform-based work. The relationship between migration and labor exploitation. The impact of data-driven technologies on employment. The influence of financial technologies on labor markets. New forms of labor extraction created through digital platforms. Power structures operating within platform ecosystems. Researchers will use ethnographic methods to investigate both migrant workers lived experiences and the broader platform economy in Finland. Main Responsibilities of the Doctoral Researcher The successful candidate will undertake an independent doctoral research project while contributing to the broader MAPS research agenda. Primary responsibilities include: Conduct Independent Doctoral Research The researcher will develop and complete a doctoral dissertation focused on topics including: Critical migration studies Sociology of work Platform labor Digital labor Migration and employment Platformization in Finland Develop Innovative Research Methods The researcher will participate in developing ethnographic approaches to studying: Migrant workers Platform companies Digital labor ecosystems Data-driven employment systems Produce Academic Publications The successful applicant will complete an article-based PhD , producing high-quality scholarly publications based on empirical research. Participate in Project Activities Additional responsibilities include: Organizing seminars and project events Participating in research communication Collaborating with project members Supporting dissemination of findings Teaching Duties The appointment includes limited teaching responsibilities, accounting for up to 5% of annual working time . Research Areas of Interest Applicants are encouraged to propose research that aligns with the overall project while incorporating their own academic interests and expertise. Relevant research themes include: Platform economy Digital labor Sociology of work Migration studies Ethnographic research Critical migration theory Platform capitalism Gig economy Labor precarity Data-driven employment Digital transformation Platform governance Who Should Apply? The University of Helsinki welcomes applicants with strong academic backgrounds who are interested in interdisciplinary social science research. Applicants should demonstrate: Strong research motivation Independent thinking Excellent analytical ability Academic writing skills Interest in migration and labor research Commitment to completing a doctoral degree The university encourages applications from individuals from diverse backgrounds and promotes an inclusive academic environment. Eligibility Requirements To be considered, applicants must meet the following requirements: Educational Qualifications Applicants should hold a Master s degree in a field relevant to the project, such as: Sociology Human Geography Cultural Studies Social and Cultural Anthropology Or another closely related discipline Doctoral Admission Applicants must: Already have the right to pursue doctoral studies at the University of Helsinki before employment begins, or Obtain doctoral study rights within the six-month probationary period. Preferred Academic Expertise The selection committee particularly values applicants with knowledge in one or more of the following areas: Tech-finance Platformization Digitalization Critical migration studies Decolonial theory Migration and labor Legal theory Labor law Skills Required Successful applicants should possess: Excellent written English Strong communication skills Outstanding analytical abilities Independent research capability Motivation to conduct ethnographic research Employment Conditions The appointment offers a comprehensive employment package. Key details include: Fixed-term contract of 3.5 years Start date: 1 October 2026 Six-month probation period Standard Finnish pension benefits Occupational healthcare University employee benefits Residence Requirement The successful candidate is expected to reside in Finland during the employment period. Required Application Documents Applicants must submit the following PDF documents: 1. Motivation Letter Maximum one page describing: Interest in the project Relevant background Suitability for the position 2. Research Plan Maximum two pages (including bibliography), outlining: Proposed doctoral research Methodology Relevance to the MAPS project 3. Curriculum Vitae (CV) A detailed academic CV highlighting: Education Research experience Publications Skills Academic achievements Click HERE to read more. Selection Process Applications will be evaluated based on: Academic qualifications Motivation Research proposal Previous academic performance Relevant expertise Interview performance Shortlisted candidates will be interviewed during August 2026 . Important Dates Event Date Application Deadline 10 August 2026 (23:59 Helsinki Time) Interviews August 2026 Employment Starts 1 October 2026 Contract Duration 3.5 Years Why Apply? This doctoral opportunity offers numerous advantages for aspiring researchers, including: Fully funded doctoral employment Research at one of Europe s leading universities Work within a prestigious Research Council of Finland project Supervision by internationally recognized researchers Opportunity to conduct impactful migration and labor research Participation in innovative ethnographic research Teaching experience Access to Finland s world-class academic environment University employment benefits Strong interdisciplinary research network APPLY HERE About the University of Helsinki The University of Helsinki is internationally recognized for excellence in research and education. It actively promotes diversity, equality, accessibility, and inclusion while fostering innovative, interdisciplinary scholarship addressing today s global challenges. Researchers benefit from an intellectually stimulating environment, international collaborations, and excellent research infrastructure. Conclusion The Doctoral Researcher in the Social Sciences position at the University of Helsinki represents an exceptional opportunity for aspiring scholars interested in migration, sociology, digital labor, and platform studies. Through the MAPS project, successful candidates will contribute to groundbreaking research examining how digital platforms reshape labor markets and migrant experiences while earning a doctoral degree from one of Europe s most respected universities. With a fully funded 3.5-year appointment, strong academic mentorship, opportunities for independent research, teaching experience, and access to Finland s outstanding research environment, this doctoral position is ideal for motivated social science graduates seeking to make meaningful contributions to the future of work, migration, and digital society. Applicants interested in this opportunity should prepare their application materials carefully and submit them before the official deadline. Click HERE for more scholarship opportunities. title: Economic Growth Internship at Greater Washington Partnership 2026 in Washington, DC (Paid Opportunity – $20 Per Hour)

The internship provides participants with meaningful professional experience by allowing them to work alongside policy experts, business leaders, government officials, nonprofit organizations, and economic development professionals. Interns will contribute to research, stakeholder engagement, event coordination, and strategic initiatives designed to strengthen economic competitiveness across Maryland, Virginia, and Washington, DC. Unlike traditional nonprofit organizations, the Partnership serves as a bridge between the public, private, and nonprofit sectors. It convenes leaders from business, government, education, and community organizations to solve regional challenges and promote sustainable economic growth. This internship offers significantly broader exposure by allowing participants to contribute to: Public-private partnerships Economic research Entrepreneurship ecosystems Regional competitiveness Policy development Innovation strategy Stakeholder engagement Economic inclusion Participants gain insight into how large-scale economic initiatives are developed and implemented while building relationships with influential leaders from multiple sectors. title: CGD Research Analyst Job 2026 in London: £46,725–£51,187 Global Development Research Role
summary: The Center for Global Development is recruiting a Research Analyst in London to support its work with the Smart Buys Alliance, an international collaboration focused on identifying and promoting highly cost-effective development interventions. This full-time, mid-level position combines empirical research, quantitative analysis, policy writing, project coordination and event support. The successful candidate will help examine how bilateral donors, development agencies and governments use evidence on cost-effectiveness when making funding and policy decisions. The Research Analyst will be based in London and is expected to work from CGD’s office at least three days each week. The position offers an annual salary of £46,725–£51,187 , together with additional benefits. The role is expected to begin as soon as possible and will initially continue until 29 February 2028 . An extension may be possible, depending on the availability of funding. Applications close on 6 August 2026 at 5:00 PM British Summer Time . CGD Research Analyst Job 2026 Overview Key details of the opportunity include: Position: Research Analyst Organisation: Center for Global Development Project: Smart Buys Alliance Location: London, United Kingdom Employment type: Full-time Career level: Mid-level Salary: £46,725–£51,187 per year, plus benefits Start date: As soon as possible Contract duration: Fixed term until 29 February 2028 Extension: Subject to funding availability Posting date: 23 July 2026 Application deadline: 6 August 2026 at 5:00 PM BST Office requirement: At least three days per week Work-authorisation requirement: Right to live and work in the United Kingdom About the Center for Global Development The Center for Global Development, commonly known as CGD, is an independent, non-partisan and nonprofit policy research organisation with offices in Washington, DC, and London. CGD conducts empirical research on policies, institutions and financial decisions that affect low- and middle-income countries. Its work examines how governments, international organisations, corporations, development agencies and financial institutions can contribute to more inclusive and sustainable development. The organisation combines research with engagement across the global policy community. Rather than producing analysis solely for academic audiences, CGD seeks to translate research findings into practical recommendations that can influence development policy, financing and implementation. Its work often sits at the intersection of: Development economics Public policy International finance Aid effectiveness Global institutions Poverty reduction Evidence-based decision-making Development cooperation The Research Analyst will support this wider mission by contributing to work on how development organisations identify, assess and use evidence about cost-effective interventions. About the Smart Buys Alliance The Smart Buys Alliance connects development agencies, philanthropic organisations and research institutions seeking to increase investment in effective development interventions. The alliance promotes the use of evidence when governments and donors decide how to allocate limited development resources. Its work is particularly concerned with identifying interventions that can produce substantial positive outcomes relative to their costs. The alliance operates through three principal areas of work. Developing On-Demand Smart Buy Lists The Smart Buys Alliance supports the development of lists identifying development interventions with strong evidence of cost-effectiveness. These resources are intended to help funders and policymakers compare options and direct resources toward programmes that are likely to deliver significant results. Supporting Implementation and Evidence Building Identifying an effective intervention is only one part of the process. The alliance also supports implementation and encourages donors to coordinate their efforts to strengthen the evidence base. This may involve examining how interventions perform in different settings, identifying implementation constraints and understanding whether the results of one programme can be reproduced elsewhere. Convening a Community of Practice The alliance brings together policymakers, researchers, funders and development practitioners to exchange evidence, experience and practical lessons. The Smart Buys Alliance is a collaboration involving: Center for Effective Global Action Cooperation Globale Center for Global Development Global Poverty Research Lab Abdul Latif Jameel Poverty Action Lab Participating donor agencies and partners The Research Analyst will support CGD’s contribution to this partnership. Purpose of the Research Analyst Position The Research Analyst will provide analytical, operational and administrative support to CGD’s Smart Buys Alliance work. The role is intended to help the project deliver accurate, timely and policy-relevant research outputs. It is not limited to data analysis: the selected candidate will also contribute to writing, coordination, stakeholder engagement and the organisation of policy events. The Research Analyst will report to Michelle Rao, Fellow at CGD Europe , and work closely with members of the broader research team. The role requires someone who can move comfortably between detailed analytical work and practical project coordination. On one day, the Analyst may be cleaning a dataset or reviewing causal-inference evidence; on another, they may be revising a policy report, coordinating a roundtable or arranging travel for project partners. Research and Analytical Responsibilities Analysing Donor Use of Cost-Effectiveness Evidence A major component of the role will involve examining how donor agencies engage with and use evidence about cost-effective development interventions. The Research Analyst may help investigate questions such as: How do donor agencies define cost-effectiveness? What evidence do they use when selecting interventions? How consistently is evidence incorporated into funding decisions? What organisational factors encourage or prevent evidence use? How can the use of cost-effectiveness evidence be monitored? How might donor practices change over time? Work in this area may include: Literature reviews Data collection Data extraction Dataset construction Data cleaning Quantitative analysis Textual analysis Review of policy and organisational documents Textual Analysis Using Large Language Models The position may involve using large language models to support the analysis of textual data. This could include examining development strategies, policy documents, donor reports or other materials to identify patterns in how organisations discuss and apply evidence. Candidates with prior experience using large language models for evidence synthesis or textual analysis will have an advantage. However, this experience is identified as beneficial rather than mandatory. Applicants should understand that the role requires analytical judgement. Tools may assist with large volumes of text, but conclusions must still be transparent, credible and suitable for policy research. Research on Evidence Use in Development Policy The Research Analyst will support wider research on how evidence informs international development policy. This may include: Original data analysis Quantitative research Cost-effectiveness analysis Heterogeneity analysis Causal-inference methods Evidence synthesis Interpretation of empirical findings Preparation of charts and visualisations Heterogeneity analysis may be used to examine whether an intervention produces different effects across populations, countries or implementation settings. Cost-effectiveness analysis may involve comparing the costs and outcomes of different interventions to assess which approaches offer greater value. Drafting Research Outputs The Research Analyst will contribute to drafting and revising: Academic or policy papers Research reports Policy briefs Blogs Monitoring products Analytical summaries Supporting materials for stakeholders The selected candidate must be able to communicate technical findings clearly without flattening the nuance out of them. Policy audiences generally need clarity, not a statistical fog bank. The Analyst will work under the guidance of the Research Fellow and in collaboration with the wider research team. Monitoring Evidence-Use Initiatives The role also involves tracking initiatives intended to increase the use of evidence by: Development organisations Bilateral agencies Governments Donor institutions Research organisations This may require maintaining structured records, following institutional developments and synthesising information from multiple organisations or processes. Convenings and Policy-Engagement Responsibilities Research is only useful when it reaches the people making decisions. The Research Analyst will therefore contribute to workshops, roundtables and other policy-engagement activities. Planning Events The successful candidate will support the planning and organisation of: Workshops Roundtable discussions Research launches Partner meetings Policy events Stakeholder consultations Responsibilities may include preparing timelines, maintaining participant lists, coordinating invitations and ensuring that logistical arrangements are completed. Meeting Coordination The role requires coordinating meetings among participants based in different countries and time zones. The Research Analyst may need to: Identify suitable time-zone options Liaise with participants Manage calendars Confirm attendance Circulate meeting materials Maintain schedules Follow up on agreed actions Strong attention to detail is important because international coordination has a peculiar ability to turn one missing calendar invitation into a minor diplomatic incident. Travel Arrangements The Research Analyst will support travel planning for partners and participants attending Smart Buys Alliance events. This may include coordinating itineraries, gathering traveller information and communicating logistical arrangements. Required Academic Qualifications Applicants must hold a master’s degree in one of the following areas: Economics Public policy International development Development economics A closely related discipline The position requires advanced analytical training, particularly because the successful candidate will work with empirical research, quantitative methods and policy evidence. Required Professional Experience Candidates must have at least four years of professional experience in economic or public-policy analysis related to international development. Relevant experience may have been gained in: Policy research organisations Universities International organisations Government institutions Development agencies Think tanks Consulting organisations NGOs Philanthropic foundations Applicants should demonstrate meaningful responsibility for analytical work rather than only general exposure to development projects. Research and Quantitative Skills Candidates must have strong research and quantitative analytical skills. They should have experience designing and conducting empirical research in an academic or professional environment. Expected capabilities include: Structuring research questions Reviewing relevant literature Working with quantitative datasets Cleaning and validating data Applying appropriate analytical methods Interpreting findings Communicating limitations Producing credible research outputs Knowledge of causal-inference methods is required. This may include familiarity with methods used to estimate the effects of programmes or policies and distinguish causal relationships from simple correlations. Required and Desirable Software Skills Applicants should be able to conduct quantitative analysis and produce visualisations using: R Stata Experience with the following is an advantage: Python Git Large language models Textual-analysis tools Evidence-synthesis methods Candidates should explain how they have used relevant tools in actual research rather than merely listing software names in their CV. Writing and Communication Skills Excellent written communication is required. The successful applicant must be able to summarise complicated empirical findings clearly and concisely for policy audiences. Strong candidates will demonstrate the ability to: Write logically structured research outputs Explain quantitative findings in accessible language Distinguish evidence from interpretation Tailor writing to different audiences Revise work in response to feedback Maintain accuracy while remaining concise Applicants must submit a writing sample, making the quality and relevance of that document particularly important. Organisational and Coordination Experience Candidates should have experience supporting: Committees Working groups Research partnerships Multi-stakeholder processes Cross-institutional initiatives Experience in professional communications, social-media management or event coordination is also relevant. The role requires a person who can manage research responsibilities alongside operational tasks without allowing either side of the job to drift into chaos. Applicants should therefore demonstrate: High attention to detail Ability to manage multiple deadlines Strong calendar and scheduling skills Experience maintaining shared documents Clear and reliable communication Ability to coordinate across institutions Confidence working across time zones Collaboration and Working Style The Research Analyst will work with colleagues and partners from several institutions. CGD is seeking someone with a collaborative and team-oriented working style who can contribute effectively across organisational boundaries. The successful candidate should be able to: Work independently when necessary Seek guidance appropriately Share information with colleagues Respond constructively to feedback Coordinate with external partners Adapt to changing project priorities Maintain professional relationships across institutions Salary and Benefits The annual salary range is: £46,725–£51,187 The appointment also includes excellent benefits, although the vacancy information provided does not list the individual benefit components. The exact salary offered within the range will likely depend on the successful candidate’s experience and qualifications. Contract Duration and Start Date The successful candidate is expected to begin as soon as possible. The position is fixed term and will run until: 29 February 2028 An extension may be possible if additional funding becomes available. Applicants should not assume that an extension is guaranteed. London-Based Hybrid Working Arrangement The position is based in London. The successful candidate must live within commutable distance of CGD’s offices in the SW1 area and attend the office at least three days per week . The position should therefore not be treated as a fully remote opportunity. Applicants should consider the practical implications of commuting to central London before applying. Right-to-Work Requirement Candidates must already have, or be able to obtain, the legal right to live and work in the United Kingdom. The vacancy does not state that visa sponsorship will be provided. Applicants requiring sponsorship should confirm the organisation’s policy before relying on this position as a route to UK work authorisation. Application Requirements Interested candidates must submit: A current CV A cover letter A writing sample Preparing the CV The CV should clearly demonstrate: Relevant academic qualifications At least four years of applicable experience Quantitative research responsibilities Experience with R and Stata Knowledge of causal-inference methods Policy-writing experience Coordination or event-management responsibilities Preparing the Cover Letter The cover letter should explain how the applicant meets the position’s requirements. Candidates should provide specific examples of: Empirical research they have conducted Development-policy questions they have analysed Datasets they have cleaned or managed Quantitative methods they have applied Research they have translated for policy audiences Multi-stakeholder processes they have supported Competing deadlines they have successfully managed Selecting a Writing Sample The writing sample should demonstrate the ability to communicate research clearly. A strong sample may include: A policy brief A research report An analytical blog An academic paper section A development-policy publication Applicants should choose a sample that reflects their own contribution and is relevant to the role. Manual Application Review CGD states that applications will be reviewed manually. No artificial-intelligence system or automated filter will be used to screen applicants. Candidates should still tailor their materials carefully, but they do not need to construct their CV around an imaginary robot guarding the door with a keyword clipboard. Equal Opportunity Statement CGD Europe is an equal-opportunity employer committed to a collaborative, diverse and inclusive workplace. Applicants will be considered without discrimination based on characteristics including: Race Colour Creed National origin Ancestry Gender Gender identity or expression Parental status Veteran status Marital status Disability Religious affiliation Political affiliation Age Sexual orientation Selection will be based on the requirements of the position and the applicant’s qualifications and experience. Application Deadline Applications must be submitted by: 6 August 2026 at 5:00 PM BST Candidates should submit before the closing time to avoid last-minute technical problems. International applicants should note that the deadline is stated in British Summer Time. APPLY HERE Conclusion The CGD Research Analyst position offers an experienced international-development researcher the opportunity to contribute to influential work on cost-effectiveness and evidence use in development policy. The role combines quantitative research, policy writing, large-scale textual analysis, coordination and stakeholder engagement. It is especially suited to candidates who can move confidently between data, ideas and the practical machinery of international collaboration. Applicants need a relevant master’s degree, at least four years of professional experience, strong quantitative skills and experience using R and Stata. Knowledge of causal inference is required, while experience with Python, Git, evidence synthesis or large language models would strengthen an application. The position is based in London, offers a salary of £46,725–£51,187 , and will continue until 29 February 2028 , with a possible extension depending on funding. Qualified candidates must submit their CV, cover letter and writing sample by 6 August 2026 at 5:00 PM BST . To discover more job opportunities, VISIT HERE . title: Luce/ACLS Program in China Studies 2026–2027: Fully Funded Fellowships, Travel Grants, and Research Opportunities for Early-Career Scholars in the United States and Canada
summary: The Luce/ACLS Program in China Studies 2026–2027 is now accepting applications for its prestigious fellowships and grants designed to strengthen and reshape the future of China studies across North America. Administered by the American Council of Learned Societies (ACLS) and generously supported by the Henry Luce Foundation, the program provides substantial funding, research support, mentorship opportunities, and professional development resources for graduate students, early-career scholars, and researchers working in China studies. As the academic landscape surrounding China continues to evolve, scholars increasingly face numerous challenges, including limited access to research materials, shrinking funding opportunities, geopolitical tensions, and barriers to academic collaboration. Recognizing these challenges, ACLS has redesigned the Luce/ACLS Program in China Studies to better support researchers and ensure that China studies remains a vibrant, inclusive, and globally relevant field. The program offers multiple funding opportunities ranging from travel grants to flexible and long-term fellowships, allowing scholars to pursue innovative research while contributing to public understanding of China, its history, cultures, societies, and global influence. About the Luce/ACLS Program in China Studies Since its establishment in 2012, the Luce/ACLS Program in China Studies has played an important role in supporting scholars throughout North America, particularly those in the early stages of their academic careers. Following extensive consultations with researchers, universities, and stakeholders in 2023, ACLS redesigned the program to respond to the changing needs of the discipline. The new structure focuses not only on providing financial assistance but also on building stronger academic networks, expanding access to research resources, encouraging interdisciplinary collaboration, and fostering publicly engaged scholarship. The program seeks to ensure that future generations of scholars have the resources, support systems, and institutional capacity necessary to produce meaningful research that benefits both academia and the broader public. Program Objectives The redesigned Luce/ACLS Program in China Studies is guided by three major goals: 1. Expand the Field of China Studies The program seeks to broaden China studies by: Supporting diverse scholarly voices Encouraging new perspectives on Chinese history, society, and culture Promoting scholarship from researchers with varied educational and professional backgrounds Supporting institutions that have historically had fewer opportunities in the field 2. Build Sustainable Academic Infrastructure The initiative aims to address long-term challenges affecting China studies by: Building stronger scholarly networks Supporting collaboration among researchers Developing lasting academic infrastructure Creating strategies that strengthen the future of the discipline 3. Promote Public Understanding The program encourages research that helps the wider public better understand: China s history Chinese cultures Contemporary Chinese society China s influence on global communities China s impact on international politics, economics, and culture Fellowship and Grant Opportunities Available for 2026–2027 Applicants may apply for several funding opportunities depending on their academic stage and research needs. 1. Luce/ACLS Travel Grants in China Studies These grants support travel related to China studies research. Grant Value Up to $5,000 Duration Travel may take place at any point during a 12-month period. Intended Applicants Graduate students Non-tenure-track researchers These grants are ideal for scholars who need to: Visit archives Conduct field research Access specialized collections Collaborate with other researchers Participate in research-related activities 2. Flexible Early Career Fellowships Designed specifically for scholars with demanding teaching or service responsibilities. Fellowship Benefits $15,000 stipend No leave from employment is required These fellowships allow recipients to: Conduct research Complete writing projects Prepare journal articles Develop books and manuscripts Advance scholarly publications This opportunity is particularly valuable for faculty members whose teaching or institutional duties make long-term research leave difficult. 3. Long-Term Early Career Fellowships These fellowships provide significant support for scholars who need dedicated time for research. Fellowship Duration Four to nine months Fellowship Funding Minimum stipend: $20,000 Maximum stipend: $45,000 Recipients are expected to take full leave from university responsibilities in order to focus exclusively on research and writing leading toward a major scholarly publication. Supported Academic Fields The Luce/ACLS Program supports research in: Humanities Interpretive social sciences Importantly: There are no restrictions regarding research methodology. There are no restrictions regarding historical time periods. Researchers are encouraged to pursue innovative, interdisciplinary, and creative scholarship. Publicly Engaged Scholarship One of the defining features of the Luce/ACLS Program is its commitment to making academic knowledge accessible to wider audiences. Applicants are strongly encouraged to design research projects that: Inform public understanding Increase public engagement with scholarship Make humanistic knowledge more accessible Demonstrate broader societal relevance ACLS believes that scholarly knowledge should serve the public good rather than remain confined within academic institutions. Mentorship and Professional Networking Beyond financial support, fellows gain access to valuable networking opportunities. The program hosts: Mentorship activities Professional networking events Alumni engagement Community-building opportunities A networking and mentorship event will be organized alongside the Association for Asian Studies Annual Conference. Fellows selected for the 2026–2027 cohort will receive additional information in January 2027. Luce/ACLS China Studies Digital Mapping Project An important component of the program is the Luce/ACLS China Studies Digital Mapping Project. This initiative seeks to improve scholarly access to important research materials by providing: A directory of significant Sinophone collections located outside mainland China A common access plan that helps researchers locate collections across participating institutions Best-practice resources for digitizing and preserving print collections The Digital Mapping Project strengthens research infrastructure while improving long-term access to valuable historical and cultural resources. Commitment to Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion The Luce/ACLS Program recognizes diversity as an essential component of academic excellence. The program actively seeks applicants representing diverse: Academic disciplines Institutional affiliations Educational backgrounds Personal experiences Research topics Historical periods Scholarly methodologies Applications are welcomed without discrimination based on: Race Ethnicity Gender Sexual orientation Religion National origin Disability Age Other personal identities Selection is based solely on academic merit and program eligibility. Benefits of the Luce/ACLS Program Successful applicants will benefit from: Funding of up to $45,000 Research support Travel funding Dedicated writing time Professional mentorship Academic networking opportunities Participation in scholarly communities Access to valuable research resources Increased opportunities for publication Enhanced professional development Interested applicants should click HERE to apply by selecting a favourable term of their choice and learn more. Application Deadline The following competitions share the same application deadline: Luce/ACLS Early Career Fellowships in China Studies – Flexible Luce/ACLS Early Career Fellowships in China Studies – Long-Term Luce/ACLS Travel Grants in China Studies Application Deadline: November 5, 2026 Applicants are encouraged to begin preparing their application materials well before the deadline and carefully review the eligibility requirements for their chosen competition. Contact Information Applicants seeking additional information should review the respective competition pages or contact the program through the ACLS China Studies office. Institutional administrators, including Offices of Sponsored Projects, are also encouraged to consult the general guidance provided by ACLS regarding institutional application procedures. Conclusion The Luce/ACLS Program in China Studies continues to serve as one of North America s most significant funding initiatives for scholars studying China within the humanities and interpretive social sciences. Through its redesigned fellowships, grants, mentorship programs, and digital resource initiatives, ACLS is investing in the future of China studies by empowering researchers, promoting inclusive scholarship, and strengthening the academic infrastructure needed for long-term success. Whether you are a graduate student seeking travel support, an early-career academic balancing teaching responsibilities, or a recent PhD looking for dedicated research time, this program provides valuable financial assistance and professional opportunities to advance your scholarship. Interested applicants should carefully review the eligibility requirements and submit their applications before the November 5, 2026 deadline. title: THRIVE Project 2026: Transforming Women’s Economic Empowerment, Climate Resilience, and Inclusive Livelihoods in Nigeria
summary: Women continue to play a vital role in driving economic growth, strengthening families, and building resilient communities. However, many women—particularly those living in underserved communities and women with disabilities—still face significant barriers to accessing finance, markets, productive resources, and leadership opportunities. Addressing these challenges requires targeted interventions that promote gender equality, economic inclusion, and sustainable development. The Transforming Her Resilience, Inclusion and Value in Economies (THRIVE) project is one such initiative designed to empower women economically while transforming the systems that continue to limit their participation. Implemented by the Women Environmental Programme (WEP) as part of the Christian Aid Women Transforming Economies Signature Programme in Nigeria , THRIVE seeks to create lasting change by improving women s access to dignified work, financial opportunities, entrepreneurship support, climate-resilient livelihoods, and decision-making processes. This comprehensive 48-month initiative focuses on strengthening local economic systems so that women can thrive as entrepreneurs, farmers, business owners, and community leaders while promoting inclusive economic development. About the THRIVE Project The Transforming Her Resilience, Inclusion and Value in Economies (THRIVE) project is a four-year development initiative aimed at transforming local economies to become more inclusive, equitable, and sustainable for women. The project recognizes that meaningful economic empowerment goes beyond providing financial support. It also requires changing the structures, relationships, policies, and social norms that prevent women from fully participating in economic activities. Through collaboration with community stakeholders, financial institutions, women s organizations, policymakers, and development partners, THRIVE seeks to build economic systems that value women s contributions and ensure equal access to opportunities. The project is funded by Christian Aid and implemented by the Women Environmental Programme (WEP) in Nigeria. Project Duration The THRIVE project will run for: 48 months (4 years) This extended implementation period allows for sustainable interventions, long-term capacity building, and measurable improvements in women s economic participation and resilience. Geographic Focus The THRIVE project is currently being implemented in: Nasarawa Eggon Local Government Area (LGA) Nasarawa State Nigeria Communities participating in the project are carefully selected through detailed assessments that consider: Gender inclusion Disability inclusion Market accessibility Community needs Economic vulnerability This approach ensures that resources reach women and communities with the greatest need. The Challenges THRIVE Seeks to Address Across many communities, women continue to face structural inequalities that prevent them from achieving economic independence. THRIVE aims to address several key challenges, including: Limited Access to Finance Many women entrepreneurs and farmers struggle to obtain: Business financing Agricultural loans Investment capital Savings opportunities Financial services Without adequate financial support, expanding businesses or increasing productivity becomes extremely difficult. Limited Access to Productive Assets Women often have fewer opportunities to access essential productive resources such as: Agricultural land Modern farming tools Equipment Technology Business infrastructure These limitations reduce income generation and long-term economic growth. Unsafe and Unequal Market Conditions Many women operate within markets that present significant barriers, including: Gender discrimination Limited market access Low bargaining power Poor infrastructure Unfair trading conditions THRIVE seeks to improve women s ability to participate in profitable and inclusive markets. Unpaid Care Responsibilities Women frequently shoulder unpaid domestic and caregiving responsibilities that reduce the time available for: Business development Skills training Employment Leadership Economic participation Reducing this burden is essential for achieving gender-equitable economies. Limited Participation in Decision-Making Women often have little influence over: Local economic policies Community planning Market governance Resource allocation Development priorities THRIVE supports women s participation in leadership and policy discussions that directly affect their livelihoods. Project Goal The primary goal of THRIVE is to build gender-just economies where women enjoy: Greater economic rights Increased income security Improved access to productive opportunities Equal participation in markets Stronger influence over economic policies Sustainable and resilient livelihoods Ultimately, the project seeks to transform local economic systems into environments where women can succeed without discrimination or structural barriers. APPLY HERE THRIVE s Four Strategic Pillars The project is built around four integrated intervention areas that work together to strengthen women s economic empowerment. 1. Evidence for Change THRIVE generates research and evidence on barriers affecting women to promote informed policy development. Activities include: Research on unpaid care work Studies on disability inclusion Gender analysis Policy advocacy Community consultations Evidence-based recommendations The information gathered helps shape more inclusive economic policies and practices. 2. Enterprise Development and Skills Building The project equips women with practical knowledge and business skills needed for long-term success. Support includes: MSME coaching Entrepreneurship development Business management training Digital literacy training Enterprise growth support Skills development for young women Capacity building for women with disabilities These interventions help women establish, strengthen, and expand their businesses. 3. Financial Inclusion and Market Access Access to finance and profitable markets is critical for sustainable economic growth. THRIVE strengthens women s financial opportunities by: Supporting Village Savings and Loan Associations (VSLAs) Connecting women with financial institutions Improving access to capital Facilitating market linkages Expanding business networks Strengthening value chains These efforts enable women to grow sustainable enterprises and increase household incomes. 4. Climate Resilience Climate change continues to threaten livelihoods, particularly for women working in agriculture. THRIVE promotes climate-smart economic activities including: Poultry production Apiculture (beekeeping) Dry-season gardening Climate-resilient farming Livelihood diversification Sustainable agricultural practices These initiatives help women adapt to climate change while improving food security and income generation. Who Will Benefit? The THRIVE project directly supports 300 women from various economic backgrounds. Primary beneficiaries include: Women-led Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) Aspiring women entrepreneurs Women farmers Agro-processors Women with disabilities The project prioritizes women facing economic exclusion and limited access to development opportunities. Strategic Partnerships Successful implementation of THRIVE relies on collaboration with multiple stakeholders. Key partners include: Christian Aid Women Environmental Programme (WEP) Women s Rights Organisations (WROs) Local policymakers Financial institutions Community leaders Development partners These partnerships strengthen implementation while ensuring sustainable community ownership. Expected Impact Through its integrated approach, THRIVE aims to deliver long-term outcomes including: Increased economic independence for women Improved entrepreneurship capacity Greater financial inclusion Enhanced market participation Stronger climate resilience Improved policy influence Better livelihoods for women and families Inclusive local economic development Reduced gender inequality Sustainable community growth Why the THRIVE Project Matters Women s economic empowerment is one of the strongest drivers of sustainable development. When women have equal access to financial resources, education, entrepreneurship opportunities, and leadership positions, communities become more resilient, economies become stronger, and poverty declines. The THRIVE project addresses not only individual economic challenges but also the systemic barriers that prevent women from fully participating in economic life. By investing in women entrepreneurs, farmers, and women with disabilities, the project contributes to inclusive development while supporting broader goals of gender equality, climate resilience, and economic justice. Its comprehensive model demonstrates how coordinated interventions across finance, skills development, policy, and climate adaptation can create lasting and transformative change. Visit HERE to learn more about the THRIVE Project 2026 Conclusion The Transforming Her Resilience, Inclusion and Value in Economies (THRIVE) project represents a significant investment in women s economic empowerment in Nigeria. Through entrepreneurship support, financial inclusion, climate-resilient livelihoods, policy advocacy, and capacity building, the project seeks to create lasting opportunities for women while transforming the local economic systems that shape their lives. By directly supporting women-led enterprises, aspiring entrepreneurs, farmers, and women with disabilities, THRIVE contributes to building more inclusive, resilient, and gender-just economies. As implementation continues over its 48-month duration, the project is expected to deliver meaningful improvements in livelihoods, economic participation, and sustainable community development across Nasarawa Eggon Local Government Area.
