title: The Alexander von Humboldt Foundation and British Academy Knowledge Frontiers Symposium 2027 for Early Career Researchers (Fully Funded to Germany)
summary: The Alexander von Humboldt Foundation and the British Academy have officially opened applications for the Knowledge Frontiers Symposium 2027 , a prestigious international research collaboration programme designed for early-career researchers in the humanities and social sciences . The symposium offers an exceptional opportunity for emerging scholars from the United Kingdom and Germany to collaborate on pressing global issues surrounding the relationship between humans and nature while building long-term international research partnerships. The symposium, scheduled to take place from 21–23 April 2027 , will bring together approximately 30 outstanding early career researchers , with around 15 participants from the United Kingdom and 15 from Germany , creating an interdisciplinary platform for networking, intellectual exchange, and collaborative research. In addition to fully covering participants travel-related expenses, the programme also provides opportunities to compete for seed funding to support future international collaborative research projects. If you are an early career researcher passionate about sustainability, resilience, environmental justice, policy development, or the intersection between society and nature, this symposium presents an outstanding opportunity to connect with leading researchers and develop meaningful international collaborations. About the Knowledge Frontiers Symposium 2027 The Knowledge Frontiers Symposium is a collaborative initiative jointly organized by the British Academy and the Alexander von Humboldt Foundation . The programme is specifically designed to strengthen research partnerships between scholars in the United Kingdom and Germany while encouraging interdisciplinary approaches to solving today s most complex societal and environmental challenges. The 2027 symposium will be held between: Wednesday, 21 April 2027 Friday, 23 April 2027 Before the physical symposium begins, participants will also have opportunities to engage virtually by discussing research interests, exchanging ideas, and beginning collaborative conversations that can continue during and after the event. Rather than functioning as a traditional academic conference, the symposium emphasizes interactive discussions, collaborative learning, networking, and the development of future joint research initiatives. Symposium Theme Humans and Nature: More Resilient Towards the Future The 2027 edition focuses on the broad interdisciplinary theme: Humans and Nature: More Resilient Towards the Future. The organizers recognize that the relationship between humans and the natural environment has become one of the defining issues of the modern world. Throughout history, there have been different perspectives regarding humanity s place within nature. Some viewpoints argue that humans possess the authority to manage and control nature, while others believe humans are an integral part of nature and should coexist with natural systems in more sustainable and balanced ways. Today, increasing global crises—including climate change, biodiversity loss, technological transformation, economic pressures, environmental degradation, and population growth—have intensified the urgency of reconsidering this relationship. The symposium aims to encourage participants to rethink how societies interact with ecological systems while identifying practical and innovative pathways toward greater resilience. Research Topics Participants are encouraged to explore a wide variety of interdisciplinary perspectives. Potential discussion areas include, but are not limited to: Contested understandings of society and nature Human-nature conceptualizations Environmental and social justice Sustainability challenges Ecological resilience Coupled human-natural systems Ethics and philosophy Political dimensions of environmental governance Economic approaches to sustainability Geographical perspectives Public policy development Knowledge production Narrative development Artistic perspectives on environmental challenges Interdisciplinary research approaches Future resilience strategies Researchers from diverse academic backgrounds are encouraged to contribute fresh perspectives and innovative ideas. title: UK Government Youth Climate and Nature Panel 2026: Apply to Shape the Future of Climate and Nature Policy.
summary: The UK Department for Energy Security and Net Zero (DESNZ) has launched applications for its inaugural Youth Climate and Nature Panel , a groundbreaking initiative designed to ensure that young people s voices play a central role in shaping the country s climate and nature policies. The panel will bring together passionate young people from across the United Kingdom to provide advice, share insights, and contribute directly to government discussions on environmental issues. As the UK continues its transition toward a net-zero future, the government recognizes the importance of involving younger generations in decision-making processes. Through this panel, selected participants will have the opportunity to influence policies that will impact their generation and future generations. About the Youth Climate and Nature Panel The Youth Climate and Nature Panel is a government-led initiative that seeks to strengthen collaboration between young people and policymakers. It aims to ensure that climate and nature policies reflect the ideas, experiences, and priorities of young people from diverse backgrounds across the UK. The panel will consist of 15 young people , bringing together a wide range of experiences, perspectives, and regional representation. Panel members will: Provide insight and advice on climate and nature policies. Help improve government engagement with young people. Strengthen collaboration between different generations on environmental issues. Amplify youth voices and inspire wider climate action across the United Kingdom. This initiative forms part of the UK government s commitment to ensuring that communities and young people benefit from the country s transition to a sustainable and net-zero future. Why You Should Apply Being selected for the Youth Climate and Nature Panel offers a unique opportunity to contribute to national policymaking while developing valuable leadership and communication skills. Benefits include: Contributing directly to UK climate and nature policies. Representing young people at the national level. Engaging with government officials and policymakers. Building leadership, teamwork, and communication skills. Collaborating with other passionate young people from across the UK. Helping shape future environmental initiatives. Gaining valuable experience that can strengthen future education and career opportunities. Click HERE to learn more about the UK Government Youth Climate and Nature Panel 2026. Who Can Apply? The current application round is open to young people aged 16 to 18 who are based in the United Kingdom . Applicants should: Have a genuine interest in climate change and nature. Be willing to share their ideas and experiences. Be passionate about making a positive difference. Be open to working collaboratively with people from different backgrounds. No previous experience in environmental policy or government work is required. The panel is looking for diverse voices rather than technical experts. Commitment to Diversity The Department for Energy Security and Net Zero is committed to creating a panel that reflects the diversity of young people across the UK. Partner organizations are also helping identify candidates with different life experiences and perspectives to ensure broad representation. How to Apply Interested applicants should complete the official application form provided by the UK Government. Applicants are encouraged to submit thoughtful responses that explain: Why climate and nature matter to them. How their experiences can contribute to the panel. Why they want to help shape future government policies. APPLY HERE. Application Deadline Deadline: Friday, 11 September 2026 Applicants are encouraged to submit their applications well before the deadline to avoid missing this opportunity. Conclusion The UK Government Youth Climate and Nature Panel 2026 presents an exceptional opportunity for young people to influence national climate and environmental policies while developing leadership skills and representing the voices of their generation. By joining the panel, participants will contribute to meaningful discussions that support the UK s journey toward a sustainable future. If you are passionate about climate action, nature conservation, and creating positive change, this is your opportunity to make a lasting impact. Be sure to submit your application before 11 September 2026 . For more OFY Fellowship opportunities VISIT HERE.
